1. The HERMES measurements of the cross section for the exclusive production of $\pi^{+}$, $\pi^{-}$, $K^{+}$ and $K^{-}$ mesons in the deeply virtual Comptom scattering process on a transversely polarized hydrogen target are consistent with predictions of the GPD-based model.

(i) the HERMES data on the azimuthal asymmetry in inclusive pion production are in agreement with the predictions of the Collins model; (ii) a new measurement of the azimuthal asymmetries in the production of neutral pions in the deeply virtual Comptons scattering process is presented; (iii) a new measurement is presented of the longitudinal double spin asymmetry in inclusive deep inelastic scattering off a transversely polarised hydrogen target
The HERMES experiment has made measurements which constrain the total angular momentum contributions of up and down sea quarks to the proton’s spin to be 0.18 ± 0.14 and -0.18 ±0.16, respectively.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the measurement of hard exclusive observables in deep inelastic scattering at the HERMES spectrometer at DESY.
the measurement of the spin structure of the proton and with the study of the nucleon's internal structure.

the study of hard exclusive reactions in order to constrain the information framework of the Generalised Parton Distribution, which provides a thorough phenomenological description of hadron structure.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the HERMES experiment has provided a wealth of data on hard exclusive processes which can be used to constrain the framework of GPDs, but that further measurements are necessary to fully understand the nucleon's structure.
hard exclusive measurements are a very useful and important probe of the internal structure of nucleons.

HERMES measurements of hard exclusive observables provide a unique opportunity to constrain the information contained in GPDs and thus the internal structure of the nucleon, and in particular the contribution of the quarks to the spin of the nucleon.
